Reasoning

A closed disclosure holding an agent's reasoning or plan notes, drawn quietly so it defers to the answer.

Status: draft

Examples

When to use it

  • For the reasoning an agent wrote before its answer, above that answer in a transcript row.
  • For plan notes the reader may want to check but does not need in order to act.

When not to use it

  • For the answer itself, or anything the reader must read. Use a message.
  • For tool arguments or output. Use a message's details, or a tool call.
  • For anything that holds an action. An action goes beside the answer, or in an approval when the agent is waiting on it.
  • For settings or secondary content of a view. Use a disclosure.

Accessibility

  • Use a native details element with the class on it and a summary as its first child. It starts closed: leave the open attribute off and let the reader open it.
  • The summary is text that says what is inside and how long it is: Reasoning, 14 lines, or Plan, 4 steps. Count what the reader will see, in a unit they know.
  • ds-reasoning__body holds text only: paragraphs, or the steps of a plan as a list with the numbers written in the text. Never put a button, a link the reader must follow or a form control inside.
  • Line breaks in the text are kept. Write the reasoning as text, never as markup.
  • The text is muted on the page surface. Do not place the component on a sunken or tinted surface, where muted text is too faint.
  • Enter and Space open and close the summary, and its pointer target is 44px tall. The component needs no script.
